descriptionHtml:
Approach · OAT-01 Signing In & Session Security · S19 Native iOS and Android: Face ID / fingerprint unlock, PIN fallback, keychain storage, and no unlock after a session has ended or on another device

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U2 After first login the session credential is kept in the device's secure keychain, and Face ID / fingerprint unlocks the app instead of a full re-login. … (UAT OAT-01 step 2; UAT OAT-01 Expected; TFA-94513 AC 3; TFA-94513 AC 17) — gate: blocked: TFA-94513 in progress
  • T4 App review accounts: exactly two designated emails (appconnect-test-account@roundcompanion.com, playstore-test-account@roundcompanion.com) accept a fixed, reusable code that never expires. … (TFA-94513 AC 15; TFA-94513 AC 16; UAT OAT-01 Expected) — gate: blocked: TFA-94513 in progress
  • T2 Each device signs in with its own email OTP, and a new device always needs one. Phone and computer hold separate sessions that are valid at the same time: signing in on one never signs the other out. (TFA-94513 AC 6; TFA-94513 AC 9; TFA-94513 AC 10) — gate: blocked: TFA-94513 in progress

Test design technique: Device (device) — Look at the layout and gestures at phone size or on a real device (iPhone / Pixel).

Given A TestFlight build on an iPhone with Face ID and a Play internal build on an Android phone with fingerprint, plus one device with no biometrics enrolled (reviewer case). One physician signed in once with the emailed code.

When Kill the app and reopen it; cancel Face ID; reopen on the no-biometrics device; inspect where the session is stored and the keychain item's accessibility attribute; repeat after 12 h idle (Q3). Then Sign out, reopen; sign in, Sign out everywhere from the web, reopen; …

Then Reopening asks for Face ID / fingerprint through the native prompt (not a browser passkey sheet) and opens the app without an email code. Cancelling falls back to the device PIN. The no-biometrics device unlocks with the PIN. …

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): U2, T4 (AC 16) and T2 (AC 6: a new device always needs an email code). Any re-login by email code on a plain reopen, any browser passkey sheet, a session token in WebView localStorage, a Face ID prompt or a chart after the session ended, or a second device that gets in without a code = Fail. TFA-92570 AC 3's claim of the same plugins is judged on its own in S23 (T13).

Where it ran: dev; test method DEVICE · Real device (iOS / Android); lane planned in the matrix: manual (blocked)

S19 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/OAT-01.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: dev — dev deployment, build e02167f (Deploy Convex, 2026-10-12T18:24:27Z); account and address are not written into the report; run folder runs/2026-10-14-dev.

Test method: DEVICE · Real device (iOS / Android); secondary: STATIC · Static check (build output / scan) — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on dev; Source: dev.
